meta.title: Partners in Literacy Haiti
meta.tagline: Every Haitian child deserves a book in their own language.
meta.description: Partners in Literacy Haiti builds and strengthens children's libraries in rural Haiti with Kreyòl books, technology and training. A 501(c)(3) nonprofit, EIN 87-0904773.

haiti.title: You are visiting from Haiti.
haiti.body: Teachers, library workers and community leaders can request Kreyòl books, alphabet charts and training here. There is no cost to ask.

global.title: Thank you for being here.
global.body: Every gift goes to books, libraries and training for children in rural Haiti. Your receipt arrives by email the moment you give.

hero.title: A child who reads in her own language never stops.
hero.lede: Partners in Literacy Haiti puts Kreyòl books into the hands of children who have never held one, and builds the village libraries that keep them coming back.

problem.title: We visited 32 classrooms and found zero books.
problem.body: Not one extra book. Not one bookshelf. Six rural schools, thirty two classrooms, and nothing for a child to read for pleasure. Haiti is the least literate country in the Western Hemisphere. Families living on less than $2.15 a day cannot buy books, and the private rural schools that teach most Haitian children rarely have a budget for them.
problem.stat1Label: of adults in Haiti cannot read
problem.stat2Label: of children leave school before sixth grade
problem.stat3Label: speak Kreyòl, yet almost all books are in French
problem.quote: Where there is no book, there is no reader. We start with the book.

approach.title: Three things, done properly, in one village at a time.
approach.lede: We do not parachute in. We partner with a village that wants a library, and we stay for years.

items.title: Books in Kreyòl
items.body: We publish and place easy readers written for Haitian children about Haitian life, plus the alphabet chart that took thirteen years and MIT linguists to get right.

items.title: A real library
items.body: Shelves, light, power, internet, computers and a paid library worker. A safe room where a child can sit down and read after school.

items.title: Trained people
items.body: Library workers complete an eleven module curriculum built in Haiti. Teachers learn how to read aloud, how to run a book corner, how to keep a child curious.

libraries.title: Five libraries. Three departments. One standard.
libraries.lede: We mentor a library until it can stand on its own, then we help the next village.

testimonial.quote: The only books in Kreyòl I ever had the chance to read were in a school textbook. I wish we had a big library where you could find all kinds of books. My dream is to write one myself one day.
testimonial.attribution: A young reader in rural Haiti, after receiving her first PILH book

trust.title: Where your money goes
trust.body: PILH is an all volunteer board with two part time paid specialists. Our books are purchased in Haiti when possible so the money stays in the Haitian economy.

hero.title: Fifteen dollars buys ten books. That is the whole idea.
hero.lede: PILH runs lean on purpose. An all volunteer board, two part time specialists, and books bought in Haiti whenever we can. Here is exactly what your gift does.

amounts.text: Pencils, crayons and markers for a reading circle
Ten Kreyòl children's books, or shelving for twenty
A set of three Haitian Kreyòl storybooks
A month of internet service for a rural library
Four classroom sized Kreyòl alphabet charts
A month of a librarian stipend and literacy workshops
A full set of training materials for one library worker
Computers and a power source for the Duplan project

involved.title: This work runs on people who remember where they come from.
involved.lede: PILH is an all volunteer organization with roots in Haiti and hands around the world. Wherever you live, there is a seat for you.
involved.diasporaBody: You left, but Haiti never left you. From Miami, Brooklyn, Montreal, Boston, Paris or Santiago, you can put Kreyòl books into the hands of children in the village your family calls home. Sponsor a library, fund a monthly book shipment, translate a story, or lend your professional skills for a few hours a month. Every committee meets on Zoom, in the language you prefer.

ways.title: Fundraising and events
ways.body: Run a birthday campaign, host a soup joumou dinner, make personal asks. Our Givebutter page makes team campaigns simple.

ways.title: Grants and finance
ways.body: Help discover and write grants, or join the finance and budget committee.

ways.title: Marketing and stories
ways.body: Create social media, design posters, film the stories that make people care.

ways.title: Programs and evaluation
ways.body: Design children's activities, build parent workshops, help measure what works.

ways.title: Speakers bureau
ways.body: Tell the PILH story to your Rotary club, church, school or company, in person or on Zoom.

ways.title: Professional skills
ways.body: Lawyers, accountants, librarians, teachers, technologists. A few hours of your craft goes far.

involved.transparencyBody: We publish our annual reports, file with the IRS every year, and hold the Candid Platinum Transparency seal. Ask us anything about the money. We will answer.
involved.contactCta: Tell us how you want to help

campaigns.title: Pick a campaign. Own the outcome.
campaigns.lede: Each campaign has a clear price, a clear result, and a report back with photos when it is done. Perfect for a family, a company, a Rotary club, a church or a classroom in the diaspora.

items.title: Change a classroom
items.body: Stock one classroom with a full set of twelve Kreyòl books, four alphabet charts and reading supplies. The teacher gets trained materials, the children get their first book corner.

items.title: Fund a library in a school
items.body: Turn an empty room in a rural school into a working children's library. Shelving, a starter collection of Kreyòl and French books, charts and a trained library worker to run it.

items.title: Adopt a library
items.body: Keep one existing village library alive for a year. Your monthly gift covers the librarian stipend, internet and new books. You receive that library's updates and photos, and your name on its wall if you wish.

items.title: Volunteer
items.body: Grants, marketing, events, translation, program design. Committees meet on Zoom in the language you prefer. A few hours a month moves real work forward.

items.title: Be an ambassador
items.body: Represent PILH in your city, your company or your club. We give you the deck, the story and the materials. You open the doors. Perfect for the Haitian diaspora everywhere.

campaigns.note: Campaign amounts are estimates based on our published program costs. Every campaign receives a written impact report.
